The AI model is not your problem. Your organization is.

New research from Oxford Economics makes it definitive: the number one barrier to enterprise AI is not technology. It is business readiness.

Data quality. Process maturity. Governance infrastructure. These are the factors that determine whether an AI initiative delivers value or stalls in pilot.

Fast-growth companies sit on the largest AI opportunity — but most are not capturing it. Not because they lack access to powerful models. Every organization on the planet can deploy frontier AI today. The gap is internal: messy data, undocumented processes, and governance frameworks that were never designed for autonomous decision-making.

This reframes the entire executive conversation around AI investment. The question is not which model to license. It is whether your operational foundation can support what these models are capable of.

The organizations compounding AI advantage right now are the ones that invested in readiness first and model selection second.

## Fact-check notes
- Oxford Economics research (cited by SAP) found that poor data quality remains one of the biggest obstacles to enterprise AI, and business readiness — not technology — is the primary barrier to scaling AI initiatives (source: SAP News Center, October 2026)
- Fast-growth companies have the largest AI opportunity but few are capturing it; most AI initiatives stall due to lack of process readiness, governance, and data quality rather than model limitations (source: SAP News Center citing Oxford Economics findings)
